priceSnapshot.note: The coil resolved upward. Since the midnight snapshot at 63,982.5 price has traded a 491.9-point band between 63,913.3 and 64,405.2 and now sits 415.1 points higher, a +0.65% move in just under five hours. That is the range expansion the midnight session said three consecutive narrowing boxes were building toward, and it broke to the upside. Two things went with it. Brent fell from 89.15 to 87.64 as Strait-of-Hormuz reopening headlines rebuilt, taking the oil-premium pressure off risk assets. And on the tape the flow flipped: short liquidations over the trailing window rose from $34,483 at midnight to $170,047 now, while long liquidations were flat at $11.54m against $11.56m - meaning essentially every dollar liquidated in the last five hours came from shorts, not longs. The honest counterweight is where price stopped. 64,405.2 is the session high and the 1H EMA200 sits at 64,398.89, so spot at 64,397.6 is sitting exactly on the moving average it needs to clear, not through it.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $63,750. UNCHANGED for a fourth consecutive session. The level sits 22.4 points beneath the 4H EMA200 at 63,772.43, and price has now probed 63,832.3, 63,818.1, 63,859.3 and 63,913.3 across four separate approaches without ever settling an hourly bar under 63,892.9. A settled hourly close below 63,750 means that moving average failed on a close rather than a wick, which removes the last structural floor before the 63,500 shelf and then the 63,000 handle. With price 647.6 points above the line this session it is a background level rather than a live one, but it is what the remaining dry cash is being held for.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE back above $64,650, WITH open interest holding or rising across the same bar. Unchanged from midnight. The price half is the daily EMA50 at 64,658.18 plus the $2,052,642 realized long-liquidation shelf at 64,600 - still the single largest cluster on the 24-hour tape - and the 4H EMA50 at 64,479.44 plus the 15m EMA200 at 64,492.41 stack up underneath as the first two hurdles. The trigger is now 252.4 points away rather than 667.5, the closest it has been in nine sessions. The open-interest half is the caution: OI is 2,082,197,596 against 2,085,719,907 at midnight, down 0.17% - flat, not rising - so this rally has been driven by spot buying and short covering rather than new leveraged longs. Flat OI would pass a 'holding' test but not a 'rising' one, and that nuance is why this session adds a partial tranche in spot rather than opening leverage.

liquidations.note: Over the 1,036-fill window ending 2026-08-11T11:55:52Z, $11,541,725 of long liquidations against $170,047 of shorts. The headline ratio of 68 to 1 is dominated by yesterday's flush, which is still inside the window - the RATE is the story. Against the midnight read of $11,558,117 longs and $34,483 shorts, the long bucket is FLAT (it fell slightly as old fills rolled out) while the short bucket rose $135,564. In other words, essentially every dollar liquidated in the last five hours came from a short position. That is a short-covering rally, not a leveraged-long chase. Two supporting numbers point the same way and one points against. Open interest is 2,082,197,596, down 0.17% from midnight's 2,085,719,907 - flat, so nobody is adding new leverage into this move, which is why it reads as spot-driven and relatively clean. Funding is +0.00583% per 8h, barely positive, so longs are paying almost nothing to hold. Against that, the long/short ACCOUNT ratio climbed from 1.62 to 1.68, its highest of the stretch, meaning retail accounts are once again crowding the long side - and a 1.68 skew into a resistance confluence is precisely the setup that produces a fast flush back to 64,000. The skew field carries that account ratio.

calibration.rollingRecord: The desk has now published a reduce level for seventeen consecutive sessions. It has fired exactly once, at 64,650 on 10 August morning, and was honoured the same session. The 63,750 line has survived four separate approaches across four sessions - lows of 63,832.3, 63,818.1, 63,859.3 and 63,913.3 - without a single settled hourly close beneath 63,892.9. The 64,650 add trigger has not fired for nine consecutive sessions and its open-interest confirmation clause has blocked nine would-be entries; the midnight session flagged that the clause would finally PASS because open interest was rising, and that call has aged badly in five hours - OI is now flat at -0.17%, so the clause would give a marginal 'holding' pass at best.
calibration.note: priorReduceFired is FALSE and again not close: the midnight 63,750 line was never approached, with the session low of 63,913.3 stopping 163.3 points above it. actingHelped is TRUE, and this is the first scoreable action in three sessions. The midnight seeder deployed 20 USDT of spot at 63,982.5 with the explicit argument that the 4H EMA200 was being defended rather than eroded and that open interest had turned up. Price is now 64,397.6, so that tranche is +0.65% and the reasoning held on the first of its two legs. The second leg has NOT held - open interest did not keep rising, it went flat - which is the honest caveat and the reason this session sizes its own add at 12 USDT rather than the remaining 35.53. Worth recording for the calibration file: the midnight session chose a partial deployment over a full one precisely because the evidence was mixed, and the mixed evidence was correct. Partial sizing under mixed evidence is now 2 for 2.
